newsitem.title: JAPAN: Oil majors' market share in Asia seen shrinking.
newsitem.headline: Oil majors' market share in Asia seen shrinking.

text.p: International oil majors are expected to lose market share in Asia as deregulation in the region provides local newcomers with a greater role, an energy specialist said on Tuesday.

Dennis Eklof, director of U.S.-based Cambridge Energy Research Associates told a symposium in Tokyo that a host of new players were becoming increasingly important in Asia"s oil market as moves toward deregulation and privatisation continue.
"The result will be greater competition and over time a shrinking role for the international oil majors, perhaps not in volume, but most definitely in share of the market," he said.
He said countries where state companies are in control were making moves towards reducing the levels of state involvement in downstream operations, which include refining and marketing.

However, opportunities for international players arising out of any changes may be limited by increased involvement of private local companies and the strong position of privatised state companies in supporting local infrastructure, Eklof said.
State companies remain in control in several countries in Asia, including two of the largest, India and China, he said.
In a separate speech, a senior official in the state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand Oil said small oil companies were gaining a substantial share of the Thai market.
The share of small oil firms has gradually grown from less than nine percent in 1991 to 21 percent by late 1996, said Chalermsak Juntaro, Senior Vice President-Planning of PTT Oil.
"The main reason for the rapid growth of non-majors is obviously the liberalisation of the oil industry, which stimulates particularly local entrepreneurs to join in," Juntaro said.

Traditionally, only four major oil companies -- PTT, Shell, Esso and Caltex -- had been profitable in the well-protected market, he said. "But, now almost 30 oil companies are operating in the country," he said.
